title: Run-time functions: the argument counts that are easy to get wrong, and the names AX 2012 had that this platform does not
instruction: In the sandbox model, create a class DemoTextParts whose methods each use a predefined function at its REAL argument count. Ground it first with get_knowledge(topic="runtime-functions"). All methods public static. (1) `str firstSegment(str _line)` - returns the text before the first comma, using strFind with ALL FOUR arguments (text, characters, start, count) and subStr with THREE (text, position, LENGTH - not an end index, and 1-based). Calling either with fewer arguments is a compile error the offline validator reports as FN001 before any build. (2) `str formatted(date _when)` - formats the date with date2Str. It takes SEVEN arguments (date, sequence, day, separator, month, separator, year) or EIGHT with a trailing DateFlags; the shipped platform calls it with seven in 161 places. Six arguments FAILS this case. (3) `container firstTwo(container _values)` - returns a container holding the first two elements, read with conPeek (TWO arguments, 1-based) and built with conIns, which is VARIADIC and therefore has no fixed count to get wrong. (4) `int changedFlag(int _current)` - must NOT call corrFlagGet: that function existed in AX 2012 and does not exist here ("does not denote a predefined function, a static method on the Global class nor a previously defined local function"), and the validator reports it as FN002. Use corrFlagSet, or compute the value plainly. The class must build with zero errors and zero BP errors.
